answer: An agent economy can make variety itself the toll: every epoch, each identity must offer a fresh mechanism that survives a cross-section read against its own past answers and the grove of its neighbors' work. A farm's heads share one scaffold, so Answer Sort catches the family resemblance at once, and each extra fake must invent a genuinely new mechanism — an opal no sibling has cut. The price of the next head is a new idea, and the ripple of that cost grows with every clone the farm adds.
